s1.syndrome_frame: Acute to subacute neurological deterioration with fever and focal neurological deficits
salient_findings: Hypodense area in the right basal ganglia with mass effect on head CT
T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the right basal ganglia and internal capsule on brain MRI
Pleocytosis and elevated protein in cerebrospinal fluid
Progression of neurological deficits and imaging findings despite empirical antibiotic treatment
key_facts: 19-year-old man with hepatitis C and intravenous heroin use
Transferred for evaluation of altered mental status
Minimally responsive and febrile on arrival
Glasgow Coma Scale 10
Required intubation for airway protection
Left upper- and lower-limb weakness (strength 2/5 and 3/5)
No meningeal signs
Vital signs were stable
Leukocytosis (white blood cell count rising from 10.0 to 14.6 × 10^3/µL)
Urine toxicology positive for benzodiazepines and opiates
Noncontrast head CT showed hypodense area in the right basal ganglia with mass effect
Brain MRI showed T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the right basal ganglia and internal capsule
Lumbar puncture yielded cerebrospinal fluid with 538 WBCs/mm³ and protein 81 mg/dL
Empirical IV ceftriaxone, vancomycin, and acyclovir were begun
Leukocytosis improved but fever persisted
Repeat lumbar puncture showed increased opening pressure and pleocytosis
Repeat MRI demonstrated progression with new involvement of the left basal ganglia

shortlist.label: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised patient with hepatitis C and intravenous heroin use, presenting with subacute neurological deterioration and focal neurological deficits

shortlist.label: CNS Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's immunocompromised status and presence of focal neurological deficits, along with subacute progression of symptoms

shortlist.label: Cerebral Toxoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised patient with hepatitis C, presenting with subacute neurological deterioration and focal neurological deficits, which are consistent with toxoplasmosis

shortlist.label: Brain Abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's presentation with fever, focal neurological deficits, and evidence of mass effect on imaging, which could be consistent with a brain abscess

shortlist.label: CNS Tuberculosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's immunocompromised status, along with symptoms of subacute neurological deterioration and focal neurological deficits, which could be consistent with CNS tuberculosis

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with altered mental status, fever, and focal neurological deficits, combined with imaging findings of a hypodense area in the right basal ganglia with mass effect and subsequent progression on repeat MRI, is most consistent with a brain abscess. The presence of leukocytosis, elevated protein, and low glucose in the cerebrospinal fluid also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cerebral Vasculitis
rejected.why: While cerebral vasculitis could explain some of the patient's symptoms, the imaging findings and cerebrospinal fluid results are more suggestive of a localized infectious process, such as a brain abscess, rather than a diffuse inflammatory process like vasculitis.
